evidence: app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:135 — entire home data flow built on resource(), stable only since v22 (2026-06-03)
app/src/app/pages/pokemon-page.ts:217 — resource() for core Pokémon data, :273 second resource for move tables
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:7 — @Service() decorator, introduced and stabilized in v22 (April–June 2026)
app/src/app/pages/move-page.ts:100, ability-page.ts:65, type-page.ts:97, type-list-page.ts:33 — resource() in every remaining page
reach.rationale: Zero experimental/preview APIs, but the app's whole data layer rests on resource() and @Service(), both stable for only ~5 months (v22, June 2026) — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:16-30 — HTTP access centralized behind PokeApi with caching and URL resolution
app/src/app/core/pokedex-data.ts:136-240 — data shaping centralized in PokedexData
app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:135 — but the resource() pattern itself is repeated in 6 page components with no shared wrapper
containment.rationale: Network access and data shaping are well isolated, but the newly-stabilized resource() API is spread across 6 files with the same boilerplate duplicated; a future resource-API shape change (it churned during v19–v21) would touch all of them.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:136-146 — resource() reactive params re-run the loader on every filter change with automatic cancellation; manual HttpClient plumbing would be worse
app/src/app/pages/home-page.ts:119-122 + app/src/app/app.config.ts:13 — input() + withComponentInputBinding implements the spec's URL-query filter state idiomatically (long-stable)
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:7 — @Service() is the v22 docs-recommended way to define services (angular.dev/guide/di/creating-and-using-services)
app/src/app/pages/pokemon-page.ts:339-343 — effect() used for the spec-required document title, a standard effect use
justification.rationale: Every non-trivial API choice buys something the stable alternatives wouldn't: reactive params, auto-cancellation, and URL-driven inputs that the spec demands. No gratuitous novelty; no experimental reach at all.

findings.issue: withFetch() is deprecated in Angular v22 — FetchBackend is now the default HttpBackend (angular/angular#58212, merged 2026-02-26)
findings.suggestion: Remove the withFetch() argument: provideHttpClient() alone now uses fetch; the call is a no-op and will be flagged by the v22 deprecation tooling.

findings.issue: A view signal duplicates the resource's value via effect (home-page.ts:196 `this.view.set(this.data.value())`), layering extra state on top of the freshly-stabilized resource API
findings.suggestion: Read the resource directly (data.value()) in the template or expose a computed view, removing the shadow signal.

findings.issue: The resource() loader pattern (params + loader + hasValue/error/isLoading template branches) is copy-pasted across 6 page components, so churn in the young resource API would require edits everywhere
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared helper or per-page wrapper for resource construction so the 7 call sites share one seam.

summary: The app contains no experimental, preview, or canary APIs — every call is stable in the pinned Angular v22. Its two central pillars, resource() and @Service(), were both stabilized in v22 only ~5 months ago, so it rides the newest stable surface with the residual churn risk that implies. Containment is partial (services isolate HTTP, but resource() is repeated in 6 files), one deprecated call survives (withFetch), and every modern API use is justified by the spec's URL-driven, reactive data requirements.
